title: SmartStart government-bridge people map
summary: Five SmartStart contributors have formal government or workforce-board ties; five New York officials are relevant gatekeepers but remain unlinked.

data.question: Which named SmartStart people have formal state or local government ties, and who controls plausible New York implementation interfaces?
data.method: Resolve the public SmartStart contributor roster against official government board, agency, county, city and school-district records.
data.framework: Two-tier people map separating confirmed SmartStart-government bridges from unconfirmed New York implementation gatekeepers.
data.scope: SmartStart contributor network and public workforce, education and economic-development governance.
findings: Naria Santa Lucia is a SmartStart contributor and governor-appointed member of Washington's board coordinating 34 public community and technical colleges.
Eric Flint is a SmartStart contributor and current member of San José's mayor-appointed work2future local workforce board.
Marzell Brown is a SmartStart contributor and listed mayor-appointed Cleveland-Cuyahoga workforce-board member; the listed term ended June 30, 2026.
Tracy Pierce is a SmartStart contributor and Deputy Director of the Michigan Workforce Development Board.
J.D. LaRock is a SmartStart contributor with former executive authority over Massachusetts' public workforce corporation and former state education-policy service.
Hope Knight, Ryan McMahon, Sharon Owens, Pamela Odom and Robert Simpson control New York state, county, city, district and regional workforce interfaces relevant to a manufacturing-school pilot.
No reviewed source links those five New York figures directly to SmartStart.
conclusions: SmartStart's public-government interface extends below governors into formal workforce and public-education governance.
Eric Flint is the strongest current local-government bridge because the City of San José lists him on a mayor-appointed workforce board with policy and funding oversight.
Central New York remains an implementation hypothesis, not a confirmed SmartStart location.
recommendations: Search work2future, Greater Cleveland Works, Michigan Workforce Development Board and Washington SBCTC agendas and minutes for SmartStart or WEF.
Search ESD, Onondaga County, Syracuse, SCSD and CenterState records for SmartStart, Kiva Allgood, ManpowerGroup and Rockwell Automation.
Do not merge Micron workforce programs into SmartStart without a primary source.
counterarguments: A contributor thank-you list does not prove formal SmartStart governance authority.
Public board roles may be unrelated to each person's SmartStart contribution.
limitations: The contributor post does not define roles.
The exact New York pilot school remains undisclosed.
Some board records omit current appointment detail.

caveats: Contributor inclusion does not prove decision authority.
New York people are adjacency leads only.

workflow.next_action: Search agendas, minutes, grants and contracts.
